Tip

  1. Need help? Please let us know in the SUEWS Community.

  2. Please report issues with the manual on GitHub Issues (or use Report Issue for This Page for page-specific feedback). Opening issues is limited to existing contributors, so if GitHub says you cannot open one, post the report in the SUEWS Community instead: a maintainer will turn it into an issue and can add you as a contributor.

  3. Please cite SUEWS with proper information from our Zenodo page.

4.1.4.1. Temporal Profiles#

SUEWS (Surface Urban Energy and Water Balance Scheme) uses the following profile containers in its YAML configuration. The container determines the keys; the consuming calculation determines whether values are weights, physical quantities or switches.

4.1.4.1.1. Keys and timing#

  • Daily Profile has two scalar keys, working_day and holiday; it is not a day-of-year series.

  • Weekly Profile has seven scalar keys: monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday, sunday. supy stores them in this order as indices 0–6 of the state DataFrame, whereas the df_state reference and the legacy tables describe the same indices Sunday first. The irrigation reader currently looks these values up with a day number that counts from Sunday, so the value given for monday is applied on Sunday, tuesday on Monday, and so on to sunday on Saturday; see the weekly irrigation day-order report.

  • Hourly Profile has working_day and holiday mappings, each with all 24 keys "1" through "24". Key "1" starts at 00:00 and key "24" at 23:00; the corresponding kernel indices are 0–23.

  • Ten Minute Profile, Heating Setpoint Profile and Cooling Setpoint Profile have the same two mappings, each with all 144 keys "1" through "144". Key "1" covers 00:00–00:10 and key "144" covers 23:50–24:00 (start included, end excluded); kernel indices are 0–143.

For the two-day-type containers, working_day is selected Monday to Friday and holiday on Saturday and Sunday. This selection uses the weekday only, without a public-holiday calendar.

The hourly anthropogenic profiles interpolate linearly from the current hour’s value towards the next hour’s value, wrapping from key "24" to key "1" of the same day type. get_Prof_SpecTime_inst uses raw values; get_Prof_SpecTime_mean first divides by the mean of the 24 values. Neither computes a timestep average. The irrigation reader divides by the daily sum, interpolates in the same way, then multiplies by the timestep in seconds divided by 3600. A zero daily sum gives zero in the normalising readers. Anthropogenic and irrigation lookups subtract the configured daylight-saving offset from the hour, wrapping a negative hour to 23. Snow uses the hour directly, without interpolation; STEBBS selects the 10-minute slot directly from the hour and minute, without interpolation or normalisation.

4.1.4.1.2. Fields and value treatment#

Paths below are relative to sites[].properties. heat and co2 abbreviate anthropogenic_emissions.heat and anthropogenic_emissions.co2. Defaults are the data-model values when the containing block is present and the field is omitted, not recommended site parameters. 1 / 0 means working_day: 1.0 and holiday: 0.0; other defaults apply to every entry in both day types, or all seven weekdays. Former names are shown in brackets once.

4.1.4.1.3. Defaults#

The uniform HourlyProfile default is 1/24 in both day types. It becomes a constant multiplier of 1 for mean-normalised profiles and equal hourly weights for irrigation. It does not suit the 1-to-2 population/activity scale and never enables the exactly-1 snow-clearing switch. The shipped population/activity values also have a known scale mismatch; see the population and activity profile report. Choose values for the consuming calculation: the generic 1/144 ten-minute default is read raw, while heating and cooling setpoint defaults are 0 and 100 degrees Celsius respectively.
